title: I need recommendations because my wishlist is low
author: RadiantExternal8752
selftext:
My game, developed using Codex and Claude, has had its Steam page live for about 10 days, but wishlist activity is very low. Therefore, I'm planning some changes. I've completely redesigned the Steam page. I'm also revising the trailer to make it shorter and more effective. I've also started working with a designer on the interface and backgrounds; these will also be changed. Besides that, do you have any suggestions for the Steam page?

Steam: [Dead Man's Table](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4958550/Dead_Mans_Table/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=pre_demo)

comments.author: Xxshark888xX
comments.body:
The skeleton art drifts between frames, in one frame it has the card tucked, in another one it disappears, in the next one changes the arm and so on.

This can be a big repel when noticed, also, the trailer isn't one of the best, try r/destroymygame to obtain more valuable feedback.

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body: Thanks for your commentYou're right, I'll revise the skeleton's animations from scratch. Looking at it closely, it seems like some details have been overlooked.

replies.author: thvaz
replies.body: r/destroymygame will destroy your soul if they find out you used AI.

comments.author: Water-Cheese
comments.body:
One really jarring part for me is the skeleton guy front and centre, he constantly subtly changes colours and shades, you can even see it from the screenshots. 

There also seems like there’s no variation in scenes, the whole trailer and all the screenshots are of one static scene.

In all honestly the trailer doesn't make the game look particularly exciting either. Is the only interaction clicking a card and then watching? Are there more units or is it just one guy?

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body:
I'll definitely be revamping the animations of our skeleton character. This skeleton is the signature character of our game, and it watches us play, guiding us in choosing cards. It completely depends on its own whim; sometimes it helps us, sometimes it sets card traps, and sometimes it just makes fun of us. Our game is an Autobattler style game, and the demo includes one archer and one warrior character. There are also two separate tables where the rules change, and each table has a different variety of enemies.
In our game scene, we're always sitting at a table, and the rules, cards, and enemies change at the table. That's how I wanted to create variety.

replies.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
replies.body: I've commented on some of your work before. I'm  not sure if you're fully married to the autobattler idea, but if you're not, you should maybe try to put a unique spin on a popular preexisting  boardgame. Something that requires the player to be active and have real agency.

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body: Yes, I want the game to be an Autobattler, but the player isn't as passive as it appears in the visuals. I envisioned the selected characters leveling up and improving their stats with each kill count, and the variety of boards and enemies varying with upgrades from the Skill Tree on the pre-run screen. However, I think a more active player mechanic is necessary.

replies.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
replies.body: If you keep it an auto battler. My advice would be to add as many active decisions that are actually meaningful, I think you could look to to older kotor games and dragon ages origins ( they aren't auto battlers obviously) but the combat auto plays and will basically just auto resolve on its own if they player does nothing at all. In these games the player still has plenty of "active" decisions they can make, everything from planning before the encounter, repositioning, active skills per unit. Other than that you really are just watching, and arbitrary stat increases via upgrades  are meaningless. Autobattlers on their own end up playing like old tab target MMORPG combat...but without any of the actual good stuff.  Give it some thought.

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body: Thank you so much for your comments and suggestions. I've decided that making a few fundamental changes seems most logical, especially since I think these changes are essential before uploading the demo to Steam.

comments.author: stuffedcrust_studios
comments.body: the actual 'gameplay' area only uses like 15% of the screen, the rest is darkness and some dodgy AI skelly anims, i'm no expert but this doesn't seem like the kind of thing that normally does well.

comments.author: Lordxb
comments.body: Yes, this game requires major over haul, rushing to demo on Steam was bad choice before you got the game properly animated and its core features done. You may of kinda screwed yourself with the Steam rushed out demo!!
